originality.rationale: The exact frame-bound functions and global uniqueness are openly credited to Faulhuber–Shafkulovska. The assessed claim is the distinct high-density boundary-layer profile, the three noncoalescing additive optimizer shifts log 3/log 4/log 6, and the quantified anisotropy advantage over the square lattice. Full-text comparison identified qualitative reference-point proximity but no stated sharp profiles or these constants. These formulas are an asymptotic refinement of the exact model, not a new existence/classification theorem. Because they are mathematically derivable from the earlier exact expressions through a singular-perturbation argument, historical originality has residual risk; no claim is made that the exact frame-bound formulas are new.

value.rationale: The exact positions of all three competing optimizing lattices quantify a nonvanishing design tradeoff at high redundancy. The anisotropic lattice improves the square-lattice excess condition number by a diverging factor asymptotic to n/[4(log n)^2], a natural frame-stability metric not read off from the prior qualitative optimizer ordering. The uniform boundary-layer profiles explain why the three constants differ and enable quantitative lattice selection; they are not arbitrary isolated digits.
